title: The Psychology of Everyday Things (revised as The Design of Everyday Things)
authority: Norman is a cognitive scientist, co-founder of Nielsen Norman Group and former Apple VP; this is the canonical text on usability of everyday objects.
caveats: Norman himself retracted his 1988 loose use of 'affordance' in favor of 'signifier' (2013). Examples are mostly physical products; transfer to screens is by analogy.

title: Affordance, conventions, and design
authority: Short essay by the author who popularized the term in HCI, correcting the field's misuse of it.
caveats: Opinion essay, not empirical. Distinction between real and perceived affordance was itself criticized by Hartson and McGrenere & Ho as incomplete.

title: The Ecological Approach to Visual Perception
authority: Gibson was a leading perceptual psychologist; this book coined and defined 'affordance' (first sketched in a 1977 chapter, 'The theory of affordances').
caveats: Gibson's affordances are about the physical environment and need no mental representation; extending them to software is contested. Ecological psychology itself has critics in cognitive science.

title: Technology affordances
authority: Gaver is a Royal College of Art / Goldsmiths interaction design researcher; this is the first major HCI paper to develop affordances beyond Norman's usage.
caveats: Conceptual paper with illustrative examples, no experiments.

title: Cognitive, physical, sensory, and functional affordances in interaction design
authority: Hartson is a Virginia Tech HCI professor and usability engineering author; the paper is a widely cited (hundreds of citations) response to Norman's 1999 essay.
caveats: Conceptual framework; not tested empirically. Terms are used differently from Norman's later 'signifier' vocabulary.

title: Affordances: Clarifying and evolving a concept
authority: HCI researchers from UBC; the standard reconciliation of Gibson's and Norman's definitions.
caveats: Conceptual; proposes a framework (e.g. degrees of affordance, separating affordance from information that specifies it).

title: Paradox of the active user
container: Interfacing Thought: Cognitive Aspects of Human-Computer Interaction
authority: Carroll and Rosson were IBM research scientists and founders of scenario-based design; the chapter is a foundational, much cited account of why users skip manuals.
caveats: Based on 1980s word-processor studies; modern help systems differ, but Nielsen later reaffirmed the behavior.

title: The role of a mental model in learning to operate a device
authority: Kieras (Univ. of Michigan) is a leading cognitive modeler of HCI; this is a classic controlled experiment on device models.
caveats: Small laboratory studies with an artificial control panel; later work shows model benefits depend on model type and task.

title: Mental Models
authority: Edited volume that established mental models as a research field, with chapters by Norman, Kieras, Gentner and others.
caveats: Mental model is a loosely defined construct; critics note it is hard to falsify.

title: About Face: The Essentials of User Interface Design
authority: Cooper created Visual Basic's prototype and originated personas and goal-directed design.
caveats: Personas are a design tool, not validated empirical method; critics (Chapman & Milham 2006) argue personas lack rigor and can be invented. Data-grounded personas are advised.

title: Microinteractions: Designing with Details
authority: Saffer is a veteran interaction designer and author of Designing for Interaction (2006).

title: The Humane Interface: New Directions for Designing Interactive Systems
authority: Raskin started the Macintosh project at Apple and wrote the standard critique of modes.
caveats: Some positions (e.g. quasimodes, zoomable interfaces, elimination of applications) did not become mainstream; the mode-error argument is well supported.

title: Instrumental interaction: An interaction model for designing post-WIMP user interfaces
authority: Beaudouin-Lafon is a professor at Université Paris-Saclay and ACM CHI Academy member.
caveats: Model with design-space metrics; validated through prototypes rather than controlled studies.

title: Magic Ink: Information software and the graphical interface
authority: Victor is a respected interface researcher (formerly Apple, Dynamicland); essay widely cited in design circles.
caveats: Long essay by an individual, not peer-reviewed; argues a position, partly manifesto.

title: Plans and Situated Actions: The Problem of Human-Machine Communication
authority: Suchman is an anthropologist at Xerox PARC; the book founded the situated-action approach in HCI.
caveats: Based on ethnography of copier users; debate with cognitive-planning views (e.g. Vera & Simon 1993) continues.

title: Interaction frogger: a design framework to couple action and function through feedback and feedforward
authority: Authors from the Delft/Eindhoven tangible-interaction group.
caveats: Framework illustrated by prototypes; not broadly tested. DOI and pages come from a single bibliographic record (dblp), not cross-checked on the ACM page.

title: Direct manipulation interfaces
authority: UCSD cognitive scientists; introduced the gulfs of execution and evaluation and the notion of directness.
caveats: Conceptual analysis; directness is not always better (e.g. for repetitive or abstract tasks).
